newsitem.title: USA: Hayes Wheels to buy Lemmerz of Germany for $301 million.
newsitem.headline: Hayes Wheels to buy Lemmerz of Germany for $301 million.

text.p: Hayes Wheels International Inc. said Monday it agreed to acquire 77 percent of Lemmerz Holding GmbH of Germany, Europe's leading full-line wheel supplier, in a cash and stock transaction worth about $300 million.

The combined company, to be named Hayes Lemmerz International Inc., will be a leading supplier of wheels, brake drums and rotors to virtually every major manufacturer of cars and light trucks in the world, Hayes said.
The company, which will also have a significant position in the heavy-duty truck and trailer markets, will have estimated annual sales of about $1.5 billion, Hayes said.

"In addition to enhancing our design, engineering and manufacturing capabilities, this transaction solidifies and extends our position as the leading full-line wheel supplier in the world," Hayes Chairman Ron Cucuz said in a statement.

"The combination of two of the oldest and most respected wheel manufacturers in the world will enhance the value we provide our customers because we are establishing a company that is the largest and most experienced supplier of wheels to the automotive and heavy-duty markets worldwide," Cucuz said.
"Together we will supply virtually every major vehicle producer in the world."
On completion of the transaction, privately held Lemmerz will become a subsidiary of Hayes Lemmerz.
Cucuz, 52, will become chairman and chief executive of Hayes Lemmerz International, which will be based in Romulus, Mich., where Hayes has its headquarters.

Under the terms of the deal, Lemmerz stockholders will receive a cash payment of $110 million and receive shares of Hayes preferred stock that will be convertible into 3.75 million shares of Hayes common stock.
Based on Hayes Wheels' stock price of $36.25 Monday, that part of the deal is worth $135.9 million. Hayes's shares were up $1.50 on Nasdaq.
Also as part of the transaction, Hayes Wheels will assume $55 million of Lemmerz' net debt, valuing the entire deal at about $301 million.
Lemmerz, which is based in Konigswinter, Germany, has 3,000 employees at facilities in Germany, Spain, Belgium, Switzerland, the Netherlands and Turkey.
The company, which also has joint ventures in Canada, Thailand, Brazil, India and Portugal, had 1995 sales of 676 million German marks, or about $450 million.
Horst Kukwa-Lemmerz, president of Lemmerz, will serve as vice chairman of Hayes Lemmerz and as chairman of Hayes Lemmerz Europe.
Giancarlo Dallera will be president of Hayes Lemmerz Europe Aluminum Products and Klaus Junger will be president of Hayes Lemmerz Europe Fabricated Products.
